description: SHADOWPLAY is a thick art and beauty publication from the makers of Behind the Blinds, built from photographic portfolios, interviews and essays that treat beauty as a subject across fashion, art, music and film. Each issue is released with a dozen or more alternate covers featuring artists, musicians and models. It is for collectors of photography led fashion and art magazines.

Sonshine is a quarterly parenting magazine about raising boys without gender stereotypes, with each issue built around a theme such as masculinity, clothes, bodies or books. It mixes advice articles, interviews, recipes, crafts, book reviews and puzzle pages for children. It is for parents and carers of boys who want a feminist angle on boyhood.

Spacing is a landscape format quarterly about Toronto's public realm, from transit, streets, housing and parks to urban design, civic politics and city history, with a themed feature section each issue. The latest number profiles the people and groups shaping the 2026 municipal election. It is for readers interested in how Canadian cities work and who want to get involved.

Stranger's Guide is a book like print series from Austin in which each issue is devoted to one place or theme and gathers long form reporting, essays, fiction and photography, mostly by writers from that place. The latest edition is a photography led issue on work and labour around the world. It is for readers who want literary, place based journalism rather than travel tips.
issue_label: The World at Work (22nd print issue, special photography edition)

description: STUDY is an English language publication from Paris in which each volume examines one person, place or idea through portfolios, conversations, essays, fashion editorials and archival documents, in a format designed to be kept rather than read once. Volume 16 revisits 1920s European modernist interiors through the archive of photographer Thérèse Bonney. It is for readers of fashion, art and design publishing who collect photography books.
issue_label: Volume 16 (09.26): The Old World, Living New

description: subTerrain is a Vancouver literary magazine mixing short fiction, poetry, essays and commentary with book reviews and columns on chapbooks and small press publishing. Each issue carries a featured visual artist on the cover and inside, and some numbers are built around a theme such as dreams or trash. It is for readers of contemporary Canadian and international writing with a stake in the small press scene.

Synth History is a thick, small format print zine about synthesizers and the people who use them, built from long interviews with electronic and pop musicians, producers and instrument designers about their gear, process and influences. Recurring sections ask artists for their favourite records or three quick questions. It is for synth players, producers and electronic music fans who like gear talk in a collectable annual edition.

Temple Magazine is a large format annual from Paris that gathers interviews, portfolios and essays on contemporary art, fashion, design and new media around a theme such as botanics or Japan. Each edition mixes art school graduates and emerging designers with established artists and often ships with several covers and heavily art directed typography. It is for readers who follow fashion school and gallery culture in France and Switzerland.
issue_label: Special Issue: Where Are They Now? (2026)

description: The Aficionados is a series of travel and design magazines in which each edition is devoted to a region or a kind of hotel, from family run places around the Mediterranean to Alpine properties. Each 148 page edition profiles the architecture, interiors and owners of the hotels, grouped by design register, with makers and products alongside. It is for travellers, hoteliers and interiors readers who use it as a sourcebook for characterful places to stay.

publisher_name: The Capilano Review Contemporary Arts Society
description: The Capilano Review is a Vancouver journal of experimental writing and contemporary art, running since 1972, that pairs poetry, fiction and essays with full colour artist projects, interviews and reviews. Issues are often themed or guest edited, recently on speculative feminisms and on prison abolition, and draw on West Coast and Indigenous writers alongside international contributors. It is for readers of avant garde Canadian literature and visual art.

The Dorchester Review is a Canadian journal of historical commentary and book reviews, with long essays on Canadian and British history, biography, politics and culture written from a conservative standpoint. Each quarterly edition runs reviews and features by academics, former political staff and journalists. It is for readers interested in Canadian history and conservative political argument in print.

The Grand Tourist is a hardcover, linen bound magazine that grew out of a design and luxury interview podcast, with around 400 pages per volume of long interviews, commissioned photography and travel dispatches on interiors, architecture, fashion, jewellery, art, food and hotels. Each issue appears in several cover editions. It is for readers and design professionals who follow the high end of interiors, craft and travel and want a book like object.

The Greatest is a large format men's fashion magazine published twice a year from Milan, each issue built around one theme and issued with several collectable covers. Inside are long fashion editorials by an international roster of photographers and interviews with actors, designers, artists and athletes, running well past 400 pages. It is for readers who collect menswear and fashion photography titles.

The Light Observer is a compact English language magazine about light itself. Each issue takes one idea, such as night, play or landscape, and gathers photographic series, artists' projects and essays alongside conversations with artists, filmmakers, architects and scientists about how they understand and use light. It suits readers of photography and contemporary art who like slow, essayistic magazines built around a single concept.

The Lissome is a Berlin print journal at the meeting point of slow fashion, ecology and craft, with each edition organised around one inquiry and filled with long essays, interviews, photography and artists' contributions on subjects such as wool and sheep breeds, wild tea and textile folklore. Editions run to around 144 pages and appear with two covers. It is for readers interested in sustainable fashion, regenerative design and nature centred culture rather than seasonal trends.

THE NEW ORDER is a large format Tokyo magazine on global street culture, covering fashion, music, art, skateboarding and design through long interviews and photographic editorials shot in Tokyo, Los Angeles, Paris and beyond. Each themed issue appears with several split covers, some made with partner brands and sold through their stores. It suits readers of fashion and subculture titles who want slower, in depth reportage.

The New Quarterly is a Canadian literary quarterly from Waterloo, Ontario, publishing new fiction, poetry, personal essays and author interviews, with each issue loosely themed and carrying the results of its annual fiction, essay and occasional verse contests. Issues are perfect bound and sold singly or by subscription alongside a digital edition. It is for readers and writers of contemporary Canadian literature.

The Rake is a bimonthly men's magazine about classic tailoring, watches, motoring, travel and what it calls gentlemanly living, built around cover interviews, fashion shoots, brand histories and essays on craftsmanship. It sits alongside a large online shop selling tailoring and accessories from the makers it writes about. It is for readers with an interest in traditional menswear and high end lifestyle coverage.

The Site Magazine is a Toronto journal of architecture, landscape, urbanism and design in which each volume takes a single theme and gathers essays, design projects, visual work and criticism from practitioners and academics. After a decade of numbered volumes it now appears as an occasional series of editorial publications and special issues, sold singly. It is for architects, designers and readers interested in the politics and culture of the built environment.

The Toe Rag is a London magazine of contemporary culture published three times a year, carrying essays, reviews, interviews, fiction, poetry and artists' projects, with back pages of listings, puzzles and an agony aunt. Each issue has a theme, recently the pastoral, decadence and fictions, and it is given out through bookshops, galleries and arts venues as well as by mail order. It is for readers of art criticism and literary writing who want a newsprint alternative to gallery magazines.
